title: Dr. Vidya Ram And Brothers Cold Storage And Ice Factory v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Pankaj Naqvi, J.; Piyush Agrawal, J.
disposition: Listed for service report; dedicated-feeder grievance not decided.
headnote: The Allahabad High Court recorded a writ grievance that the distribution licensee was granting a third-party connection from the petitioners' dedicated independent feeder contrary to the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, granted time for a counter affidavit, issued notice to the private respondent, and listed the matter for a service report, without construing the Code or granting interim relief.
facts: The petitioners, a cold storage and ice factory, obtained a dedicated independent feeder after paying processing fees and expenses. They alleged that the distribution licensee was granting a connection to respondent no. 4 from that feeder contrary to the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. On 24 November 2020 a Division Bench recorded the grievance and granted the Nigam time to file a short counter. Later listings allowed further time, directed a rejoinder, issued notice to the private respondent, and on 23 March 2021 adjourned for a service report. No interim relief issued.

holding_units.holding: Six listing orders record the petitioners' grievance that the Nigam was tapping their dedicated independent feeder, grant time for affidavits, issue notice to the private respondent, and adjourn for a service report, without construing the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 or granting interim or final relief.

principle_tags.application: The extract is a chain of adjournments and notice directions on a dedicated-feeder writ; no Supply Code clause is construed and no electricity relief is granted or refused.

not_decided.point: Whether the licensee may grant a third-party connection from the petitioner's dedicated independent feeder contrary to the Electricity Supply Code, 2005
not_decided.note: Recorded as the writ grievance; listed for affidavits, notice and service without a merits order.
